payload.description:
## Context
When an agent assigns a vault record, I want to distinguish display assignment from the canonical holder, so I can avoid a successful write whose effect disappears.
vault_view.carried currently drops ledger holder-field events, so routing legacy assign can queue an assignment that the view does not retain. Cut B changes holder-history normalization. Cut C2 leaves assign refused and names claim or unassign as the supported remedies.
## Scope
Decide assignment semantics after cut B and add a regression for the chosen behavior. Do not infer exclusion identity from a display name. The canonical identity remains the writer and session pair. No assignment implementation is part of cut C2.
## Evidence
A search of core skills, agents and fragments for assign, with two known claim matches as controls, found no assign match. The same search across projected agent and skill text found four known claim controls and no assign match. The tracker kit command reference does document legacy assignment.
payload.title: Decide vault assignment semantics without dropping holder changes

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context
When a record is created after a repository switches to the vault, I want to create, update, review, confirm, link and close it through ordinary tracker commands, so I can complete work without a writable local ledger.
The closed V3 record basicly-gtb19bg.43.28 criterion 1 promises these writes, but commands._require and vault_write._refused validate against local events before vault_write.land reads the vault view; src/basicly/owned_write.py also requires the local record. Native vault handlers currently cover comment, claim and unassign, leaving the general lifecycle unavailable for vault-born records.
## Scope
One shared adapter validates against the vault view and queues carried ledger events without local ledger writes; engine and standalone commands use that adapter. Preserve existing write gates and ownership rules. Cut C2 starts from main after cut B normalization lands.
## Evidence
The .43.28 confirmation recorded 16 passing tests in tests/test_kit_vault_write.py; its WRITES parameterization uses _seeded local records, while the create test does not perform a subsequent write on the created id. The observed missing-local rejection is tracked by basicly-ak6qrz0. Cut D and E cover migration and cutover rather than implementation of this missing lifecycle.
## Approved boundary
Orchestrator decisions on 2026-11-13 classify the 15 record forms from create plus cli._WRITES. Class 1: create, update, close, comment, review, confirm, dep, child and undep work through one shared vault adapter. Class 2: claim and unassign keep the canonical protocol; route a ledger alias only if its contract and exit codes remain identical, otherwise name the native command. Class 3: resolve and acknowledge-loss are retired in vault mode, assign has no approved vault semantics, and delete is refused; each gives a real remedy and writes nothing. Deletion names close with resolution cancelled to preserve history. Assignment semantics are tracked by basicly-ep82ws3. The reference text documents the classes and tests pin every form. Cut B owns vault_view.py, vault_share.py, vault_migrate.py and fsck.py; build C2 on main after cut B, or begin only independent contract tests until its view change lands.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When a configured repository holds a vault-born record, create, update, close, comment, review, confirm and dependency writes shall validate against the vault view and queue the intended ledger events with no local ledger event write.
- When the engine or standalone CLI performs those writes, both shall call one adapter and preserve readiness, confirmation, field, dependency and holder checks.
- When the standalone tracker is installed without the harness, init, create, claim, update, review, confirm, close and read against a local bare vault shall complete with no local ledger event writes.
- When a command is invalid or a record is absent, it shall refuse by the real cause without writing an event.
- When the 15 record forms run in vault mode, each shall match its documented class, preserve canonical claim semantics, and refuse unsupported forms without writing, with every suggested remedy parsed by its real parser.
